title: Counting the Pallets a Renew Business Asset Buyback Collection Is Charged For
content:
How the pallets the collection is charged for are counted follows the state of the agreement's collection account. That account is read as the freight charges raised on the Renew Business Asset Buyback agreement less the freight charges relieved on it by a waiver, rounded to the cent; a charge stands unsettled where that figure is above nothing, and every charge stands settled or waived where it is at nothing or below.

**Where the run leaves a part pallet and a freight charge raised on the agreement stands unsettled**
the pallets charged for are counted up to the whole pallet: the whole pallets the run fills are charged for together with a further full pallet for the part.

**Where the run leaves a part pallet and every freight charge raised on the agreement stands settled or waived**
the pallets charged for are the whole pallets the run fills together with a further half pallet for the part, whatever the size of the part.

**Where the run leaves no part pallet**
the pallets charged for are the pallets the run fills as they stand.

**Worked comparison on hypothetical inputs.** Take a run filling 3.375 pallets, which leaves a part pallet.

| The agreement's collection account | Pallets charged for |
| --- | --- |
| 310.00 USD raised and nothing relieved, so 310.00 USD stands unsettled | 4 pallets |
| 310.00 USD raised and 310.00 USD relieved, so nothing stands unsettled | 3.5 pallets |

A run filling exactly 4 pallets leaves no part pallet, so 4 pallets are charged for whatever the state of the account. A run filling 3.05 pallets leaves a part pallet, and gives 4 pallets where a charge stands unsettled and 3.5 pallets where none does, the further half pallet being the same whatever the size of the part.
